risks: Confirm LTE PRB utilization trend isn't being driven by a seasonal or temporary traffic spike that would resolve without holding spectrum.
Check device migration pace given 30.4% of devices are still LTE-only, since this LTE-only base will keep pressuring the busier LTE layer until utilization drops.
55123.lte_only_impact: The 30.4% of devices that are LTE-only continue to rely on unchanged LTE layers (L700, L1900, L2100, L2500) carrying 46 MHz total, with no reduction in LTE capacity from this hold.

55125.name: Vilas County
55125.summary: Vilas County proposes shifting 10 MHz of L1900 (blocks D, B3) to N1900, taking LTE from 26 MHz to 16 MHz and NR from 30 MHz to 40 MHz, with L700 held as the anchor. Confidence is 53, below the 60 threshold, so this is routed to Manager Review rather than auto-approved; NR congestion is already higher than LTE congestion (47.9% vs 43.0%).
risks: Confirm the 3 LTE-only sites (of 13 total, 76.9% modernized) are not concentrated in areas that would see coverage or capacity gaps once L1900 spectrum is reduced.
Check whether the isolated PCS block C5, which stays on LTE, creates any handset compatibility or interference issues with neighboring county band plans.
55125.lte_only_impact: 17.8% of devices in Vilas County are LTE-only and will continue to rely on the 16 MHz of LTE remaining after the shift, anchored on L700 and L1900.
55125.manager_note: Approve only after confirming that the 3 of 13 LTE-only sites can sustain acceptable service on 16 MHz of LTE given current LTE congestion of 43.0%, since the 53 confidence score reflects this hardware gap.

55127.name: Walworth County
55127.summary: NR congestion at 64.9% against LTE congestion at 47.8% supports carving 30 MHz of L2500 to N2500, leaving 31 MHz of LTE on air anchored on L700. Confidence is 50, below the 60 threshold, so this routes to Manager Review rather than auto-approving; 7 of 42 sites are LTE-only (83.3% modernized) and 23.3% of devices are LTE-only, close to the 30% hold threshold.
risks: Confirm the 7 LTE-only sites can absorb their current LTE load on the remaining 31 MHz (L700, L1900, L2100) without a capacity gap once N2500 takes the full 2500 band.
Check backhaul and site readiness at the 7 LTE-only sites before the shift, since they gain no NR offload from this carve.
55127.lte_only_impact: 23.3% of devices are LTE-only and will continue to rely on the 31 MHz of LTE remaining across L700, L1900, and L2100, with no capacity contribution from the 30 MHz moving to N2500.
55127.manager_note: Confidence is 50, below the 60% auto-approve threshold, driven by the 7 LTE-only sites (83.3% modernized) and 23.3% LTE-only device share sitting close to the 30% hold threshold - please confirm the Carve of 30 MHz L2500 -> N2500 is acceptable given this hardware gap.

55129.name: Washburn County
55129.summary: NR carries 1,476 of 2,135 users at 38.1% PRB utilization versus 659 users and 32.6% on LTE, and 83.3% of devices are 5G-capable, so the rule engine carves 10 MHz from L2500 to N2500, moving NR spectrum from 45 MHz to 55 MHz while LTE drops from 31 MHz to 21 MHz. All 13 sites are already NR-capable (100.0% modernized), and L700 remains as the LTE anchor alongside L600, L1900, and L2100.
risks: Confirm the 16.7% of devices that are LTE-only can still get adequate service on the remaining L600, L700, L1900, and L2100 layers now that L2500 no longer carries LTE.
Check backhaul capacity at the 13 sites can support the NR load increase from 45 MHz to 55 MHz given NR is already the more congested layer at 38.1%.
55129.lte_only_impact: The 16.7% of devices that are LTE-only will depend entirely on L600, L700, L1900, and L2100 for service, since L2500 no longer carries any LTE after the shift.

55131.name: Washington County
55131.summary: 36.7% of devices in Washington County are LTE-only, above the 30% threshold, and only 63.3% of devices are 5G-capable, so shifting spectrum from any LTE layer to NR would strand real traffic on LTE-only devices. NR utilization sits at 58.8% with headroom available, but the constraint is device capability, not capacity, so the recommendation is Hold with no spectrum shifts (LTE stays at 65 MHz total, NR stays at 75 MHz total).
risks: Track device mix trend given 5G-capable share rose from 55.6% to 63.3% over the last 12 months, and re-check the 30% LTE-only threshold at the next review cycle.
Confirm LTE congestion trend (40.9% to 38.1% over the same period) continues to hold headroom on the 5 MHz L2500, L1900, and L2100 layers carrying LTE-only traffic.
55131.lte_only_impact: LTE-only users (36.7% of devices) keep their current LTE capacity untouched across L600, L1900, L2100, and L2500, since no spectrum is being moved to NR this cycle.

55133.name: Waukesha County
55133.summary: NR PRB utilization is 71.7% versus 34.7% on LTE, and NR already carries 73,678 of the network's users versus 21,737 on LTE, so capacity pressure is concentrated on the NR side. The recommended carve moves 30 MHz from L2500 to N2500, taking LTE spectrum from 87 MHz to 57 MHz while NR grows from 80 MHz to 110 MHz, with L700 retained as the LTE anchor. Device readiness supports the move: 90.0% of devices are 5G-capable and only 10.0% are LTE-only.
risks: Confirm current NR capacity headroom at the 166 NR-capable sites can absorb the added 30 MHz before congestion drops as expected, given NR PRB utilization is already at 71.7%.
Check backhaul capacity at sites carrying the heaviest NR load, since NR user count (73,678) is already more than three times the LTE user count (21,737).
55133.lte_only_impact: The 10.0% of devices that are LTE-only will continue to be served on the remaining 57 MHz of LTE spread across L600, L700, L1900, and L2100, since L2500 is fully vacated by this carve.

55135.name: Waupaca County
55135.summary: NR congestion (49.6%) now exceeds LTE congestion (40.9%), and all 25 sites are NR-capable (100.0% modernized), supporting the proposed carve of 10 MHz L2100 -> N2100. This leaves 31 MHz of LTE on air anchored on L700, with L600, L1900, and L2500 held back as alternatives, but confidence sits at 59, below the 60 threshold, so the Carve is routed to Manager Review rather than auto-approved.
risks: Confirm device migration readiness given 29.0% of devices are LTE-only, close to the 30% hold threshold.
Check that isolated PCS block A5, left on LTE, does not create a coverage gap once L2100 spectrum shifts to N2100.
55135.lte_only_impact: The 29.0% of devices that are LTE-only will continue to rely on L700, L1900, and L2500, since L2100 is removed from the LTE layer set after the shift.
55135.manager_note: Confidence for this Carve is 59, below the 60 threshold, so please review before approving the 10 MHz L2100 -> N2100 shift.

55137.name: Waushara County
55137.summary: LTE carries more users than NR in Waushara County (2,709 vs 2,677), and NR congestion at 48.6% already exceeds LTE congestion at 42.0%, so no spectrum moves to NR this cycle. Spectrum stays at 66 MHz LTE / 35 MHz NR, with all LTE layers (L700, L1900, L2100, L2500) unchanged after the hold.
risks: Check whether the 12-month climb in NR congestion (40.5% to 48.6%) is driven by seasonal or event traffic that could ease before the next review.
Confirm device migration trends given 32.8% of devices are still LTE-only, since load won't shift to NR without the device base moving first.
55137.lte_only_impact: 32.8% of devices in Waushara County are LTE-only, and holding the spectrum split means these users see no change in available LTE capacity, which stays at 66 MHz.

55139.name: Winnebago County
55139.summary: NR PRB utilization is 64.1% versus 41.0% on LTE, and NR already carries 18,962 of 30,178 users while LTE carries 11,216, so capacity pressure is on the NR side. The recommendation carves the full 60 MHz of L2500 to N2500, taking total NR spectrum from 75 MHz to 135 MHz while LTE drops from 92 MHz to 32 MHz, still anchored on L700 with L600, L1900 and L2100 remaining on LTE. All 69 sites are NR-capable (100.0% modernized), supporting the shift at confidence 77.
risks: Confirm backhaul at the 69 sites can support the higher NR load implied by 135 MHz of NR spectrum after the shift.
Check that the 21.6% LTE-only device base has adequate coverage on the remaining 32 MHz of LTE (L600, L700, L1900, L2100) after L2500 is fully vacated.
55139.lte_only_impact: The 21.6% of devices that are LTE-only will continue to be served on the 32 MHz of LTE remaining on L600, L700, L1900 and L2100, since L2500 will carry no LTE after the shift.

55141.name: Wood County
55141.summary: Wood County holds at 70 MHz LTE / 35 MHz NR with no spectrum shift, driven by 31.7% of devices still being LTE-only, above the 30% threshold, and only 68.3% of devices being 5G-capable. NR utilization is 40.7% with headroom, but the constraint is device capability, not NR capacity, so LTE keeps its current layers (L700, L1900, L2100, L2500) and mhz load unchanged.
risks: Check whether the 31.7% LTE-only device share is concentrated on specific sites or backhaul-limited nodes that might need targeted upgrades independent of this refarm hold.
Confirm LTE congestion trend (20.9% to 27.7% over the past 12 months) isn't approaching a threshold that would force a capacity move despite the device constraint.
55141.lte_only_impact: The 31.7% of devices that are LTE-only continue to be served on the full existing LTE footprint (L700, L1900, L2100, L2500) with no reduction in LTE spectrum.
